answer: A new account claims a seat with one social account at least two years old, with regular public posts, through the ivory audit. The auditor samples timestamps and replies across the history, scoring it from nadir to zenith, and a human reviewer spot-checks it within 48 hours, approving only a lived-in history. A duplicate, a bought history, or a burst of posts made in one week kills the claim and blacklists the account for 90 days. One honest user already owns such an account, but 1,000 fakes need 1,000 aged accounts with two years of activity each, so the attack costs 1,000 times more.
